gap: None of the results ChatGPT got says that, of the four Schumacher combos it showed, only the small ones (100 A SC1281L/SC1308L and 50 A SC1305) are listed by Schumacher for 12 V lithium (LiFePO4) batteries, while the wheeled 200 A SC1309 is limited by its manual to 'only 6V and 12V LEAD-ACID (STD or AGM)' and the wheeled 150 A SC1364 to standard and AGM, so a shopper with a LiFePO4 starting battery should take the small unit, not the big wheeled one.
standout_why: Rival pages compared: clampandcrank.com (best combos, 2026-09-29) lists the SC1281 as 'Standard lead-acid, AGM and gel' with no lithium. plainprepper.com lists the SC1281 as '12 V LiFePO4' but covers no other Schumacher model. batterytrail.com names the SC1309 as a top combo pick but states no battery chemistry for any model. The cited schumacherelectric.com category page and Advance Auto SC1309 page would not load (HTTP 429 and timeout). The SC1309 manual on ManualsLib (result #6, not cited) states lead-acid STD/AGM only, but no result compares chemistry support across the models ChatGPT showed. None of them explains that lithium support depends on the 'L' suffix (SC1281L/SC1308L), and two reviews say the plain SC1308 is not LiFePO4-compatible.
decides: If the car, boat or powersport vehicle has a 12 V LiFePO4 battery, the pick is the 100 A SC1281L/SC1308L (6 V/12 V) or the 50 A SC1305 (12 V only), not the wheeled SC1309 or SC1364 that ChatGPT offered for trucks and SUVs. With a flooded or AGM battery, the wheeled units stay valid, but the SC1309 manual excludes gel batteries. If you need 24 V, only the SC1352 (12 V/24 V) covers it.
